title: Public Toilets as a Stipend Program, Not Construction
one_liner: A turnkey program manager that lets cities and business districts turn cafes, gyms, garages and gas stations into paid, insured and mapped public restrooms for a small annual stipend instead of building $225,000 freestanding toilets.
customer: Business improvement districts and downtown associations first (fast, budgeted, small contracts), then transit agencies, parks and public-works departments, and tourism boards.
problem: Public restrooms are a top complaint in every city and almost no one builds them because the capital and upkeep are brutal. One Portland Loo costs about $225,000 installed, and New York's 2026 pilot budgets about $4M for 17 units. Washington DC authorized a program to pay businesses to open their restrooms in 2018, but it went unfunded. Meanwhile there is a toilet on nearly every retail block behind a 'customers only' sign, because owners fear liability, cleaning cost and misuse, and nobody manages the risk.
solution: Run a managed 'Open Door' network. Recruit and contract the host businesses, pay a monthly stipend, provide a group liability rider or indemnity through a specialty insurance program, supply cleaning kits and signage, and put a QR code and map listing on each door. QR scans verify actual use, so cities pay for measured access and get council-ready reports on use by neighborhood and hour. A hotline handles complaints and revokes hosts who stop complying.
why_now: New York's very public 2026 pilot, including the 10-minute limit robotoilets, shows both political demand and sticker shock. Downtown business districts are fighting for foot traffic, homelessness and tourism pressure keeps restrooms a front-page issue, and smartphone QR verification makes pay-for-access measurable for the first time. Germany's Nette Toilette program has run in about 210 cities for years at roughly $34-$112 a month per business, so the model is proven but has not been productized in the US.
revenue_model: Program-management contract with the city or district: a setup fee plus about $600-$1,200 per site per year, with host stipends passed through at cost. A typical pilot of 15-20 sites is roughly $25-$60k a year. Add sponsorship by a host or utility brand and analytics subscriptions for tourism and transit boards.
non_obvious_insight: The expense of a public toilet is capital and ownership, not access. The scarce resource is liability-managed permission to use toilets that already exist. Whoever builds the group insurance, verification data and host-compliance system owns the market, and every city compares a $2,000-a-year stipend to a $225,000 kiosk.
first_30_days: Target two business improvement districts, which can approve $20-$50k pilots without a city-wide procurement cycle. Sign letters of intent from 15-20 hosts on the strongest blocks. Get a broker to quote a group liability rider. Print door stickers, build a one-page map with scan counts, and launch a 90-day pilot. Use week-4 scan data to ask the district to sign a 12-month contract and to open talks with the city.

title: Vet-Side Passport Network for Pets and Horses
one_liner: Give official veterinarians a certificate copilot that turns microchip-anchored records into error-free health certificates and a verifiable travel dossier that carriers and shippers can check before departure.
customer: Official Veterinarian practices in the UK and EU (and accredited vets in the US), plus pet and horse transport companies. Ferry, tunnel and airline operators are later payers for pre-verified manifests.
problem: Since 22 April 2026 UK-based owners must use single-entry Animal Health Certificates, 11-14 pages issued by an Official Veterinarian, instead of EU-issued passports. Vet time per certificate is heavy, the timing windows for vaccination and treatment are easy to get wrong, and a chip-number or wording error means refusal at the border. Horse shippers juggle TRACES, FEI and national passport systems separately.
solution: Software for vet practices that pulls microchip and vaccination data from practice-management systems, imports lab results, applies a country-rule engine with timing windows, pre-fills the certificate and flags errors before the vet signs. It issues the owner a portable dossier with a verifiable signature and QR code. A pre-flight checker lets shippers validate multi-animal consignments before departure.
why_now: The April 2026 EU rule change, wider TRACES digital processing, and constant UK-EU rule churn mean a maintained rules engine has recurring value. Owners are newly forced into per-trip certificates.
revenue_model: $100-190 per OV per month plus $10-20 per certificate, shipper plans from about $300 a month, and later per-manifest fees from carriers.
non_obvious_insight: The animal identity problem is already solved: microchips and horse life numbers are global standards. What is missing is trust and issuance friction, and a licensed vet is the human trust anchor. You do not need new identity infrastructure. You sell the trust anchor a better pen, and animals avoid the privacy fights that slow human wallets.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 OV practices near Dover and Folkestone, where certificate volume is highest, and 3 horse shippers. Start with the UK-to-EU Animal Health Certificate only, filling PDFs semi-manually. Charge per certificate, measure vet minutes saved and rejection rate, and publish the numbers to win the next 50 practices.

title: Factory-Slot Exchange for Transformers and Switchgear
one_liner: A verified marketplace and escrow for reassigning manufacturer production slots, the truly scarce asset, from stranded projects to shovel-ready buyers.
customer: Municipal utilities and rural electric co-ops that hyperscaler orders are crowding out, independent power producers, EPC procurement leads, and developers whose projects are stalled by moratoria or interconnection withdrawals and who hold deposit-backed slots they cannot use.
problem: Substation transformer lead times have stretched from about 140 weeks in 2023 to more than 160 weeks in 2026, and medium-voltage gear is at two to three years. Industry estimates say 30-50% of planned 2026 US data center capacity could slip on equipment alone. Slots are reserved years ahead with deposits, and when a project dies (a moratorium, a lost interconnection position) the slot is orphaned. Slot trading happens by handshake in whisper networks, with no verification and no title.
solution: A slot registry plus escrowed transfer. (1) Verify each slot with the manufacturer: spec, kVA and voltage class, delivery window, deposit status. (2) Get manufacturer consent, which is easier if you give them cleaner backlog data. (3) Match buyers using a small technical team of retired utility engineers who know which specs can be re-specified. (4) Hold funds in escrow and transfer title. Publish an index of slot pricing by spec, which is the first public price signal for the shortage.
why_now: Lead times are at record highs in 2026, and new state permit pauses (New York, Texas) are orphaning slots that speculative developers reserved. Small utilities lost their traditional access to equipment as hyperscalers bought capacity, which creates political goodwill for a neutral exchange.
revenue_model: A 2-4% fee on the purchase order value from the buyer and about 1% from the seller. Paid verification dossiers for sellers, and a subscription for the slot price index and alerts.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is the production slot with a spec, not the physical box. Because many slots can be re-specified within tolerance, a technical matchmaker unlocks supply that looks fungible only to insiders. The people hurt most, small utilities, are also the best-motivated and least-served buyers, so serving them is both profitable and defensible.
first_30_days: Recruit two retired utility procurement engineers as advisors. Cold-outreach 50 EPC procurement leads and 20 co-ops (start at NRECA-type meetings and LinkedIn). Collect five slot listings from stalled projects. Broker one transfer manually with a lawyer-drafted escrow agreement and no software. Charge the fee on that deal and use it as proof for the manufacturers.

title: Asset Provenance Ledger for AI Disclosure
one_liner: A plugin for Blender, Photoshop, Unity and Unreal that logs where each asset came from (human-made, AI-generated, purchased) and exports evidence for Steam disclosure and award eligibility.
customer: Indie and mid-size studios (5-100 staff) shipping on Steam, and awards and festival organizers who must adjudicate AI use.
problem: Clair Obscur lost two Indie Game Awards over AI placeholder textures removed before shipping. Eurogamer scored ARC Raiders 2/5 partly over AI voices. Valve requires AI disclosure on Steam. Accusations arrive after launch and the accused have no evidence trail either way.
solution: A local-first logger records per-asset origin (DCC commit hooks, generative-tool API logs, asset-store IDs) into a signed hash chain. It exports an AI Disclosure Report for Steam, award submissions and press, and offers a verifier portal for juries and a public provenance page.
why_now: Award controversies and press scoring now turn on AI use. Steam's disclosure requirement is in force. EA's owners plan AI throughout operations, which will multiply cases.
revenue_model: $15-49 per seat per month, $2-5k per event for awards verification, and $3-10k for forensic audits of accused studios.
non_obvious_insight: The dispute is not AI versus human, it is evidence asymmetry: accusers need no proof and the accused have none. A provenance log protects studios that use AI legitimately (placeholders, disclosed tools) as much as those that do not.
first_30_days: Ship a minimal Blender, Photoshop and Unity logger. Offer it free to awards-eligible entries. Talk to organizers of two indie awards about a verifier pilot, and onboard 20 studios.

title: Ground-Truth Diligence for GPU-Backed Lenders
one_liner: Independent-engineer-style diligence and monthly monitoring on the part of a data center build that satellites cannot see: the last 90 days before ready-for-service.
customer: Private credit funds, banks and ABS investors lending against GPUs and neocloud contracts; insurers underwriting delay risk; AI labs and enterprises signing take-or-pay capacity who need to know if the promised RFS date is credible.
problem: GPU-backed loans and offtake contracts are priced on a ready-for-service date. Satellite vendors (SynMax and Industrial Info Resources now cover 2,600+ projects weekly) can show steel, cooling towers and generator yards, but they cannot see the failure zone: utility permission to energize, MV switchgear energization, Level 4/5 commissioning and IST results, liquid-cooling flush and pressure tests, fiber-plant acceptance, OEM startup-tech availability. Percent complete on pay applications is front-loaded and misleading. Meanwhile GPUs costing millions per rack sit idle and depreciate while interest accrues, and lenders are capping neocloud exposure. Traditional IEs are power-plant-oriented, slow and expensive.
solution: A 'Readiness Ladder' of about 40 binary, evidence-backed milestones (utility energization letter, gear serials and bills of lading, Cx level sign-offs, IST pass/fail counts, CDU flush logs, open-punch burn-down rate, OEM startup-tech calendar). Score each project and re-score monthly. Output a probability of RFS by date and covenant or draw-release triggers. Staff it with a bench of ex-data-center PMs and Cx leads who do desk review plus quick site visits. Sell as a 2-week second-opinion product first, then monthly monitoring, integrating vendor satellite feeds as an input rather than competing with them.
why_now: Neocloud credit risk is now the topic. Lenders are capping exposure, deals are stalling on credit risk, and GPU-debt structures (including vendor backstops) are proliferating. Analyses show roughly 40% of AI data center sites with possible delays and about half of 2026 capacity slipping, while operators publicly deny it. Satellite monitoring has commoditized the exterior, which makes the interior truth the scarce and valuable part.
revenue_model: $25K fixed-fee 2-week second opinions; $40K-120K full pre-close diligence; $8K-20K/month per facility monitoring; optional success-based fee for delay-risk insurance placement. Adjacent product: retained RFS-credibility scoring for AI labs choosing between capacity offers.
non_obvious_insight: Percent complete is the wrong metric. The last 5% of a data center can consume 25% of the calendar, and it is dominated by unbounded tasks: the commissioning punch-list burn-down rate and whether the OEM has a startup technician free that month predict RFS far better than construction progress. You can only read those signals if you have run an IST. Also, the RFS date on a marketing sheet is a sales number, not a schedule.
first_30_days: Recruit 6 retired or between-jobs Cx leads and PMs on 1099 contracts. Publish a free 'RFS credibility checklist' and a teardown of one publicly delayed project. Approach 5-10 private credit and infrastructure funds with data center or GPU-lending desks. Offer a fixed-fee $25K second opinion on one live deal, delivered in two weeks, and ask permission to reference the engagement anonymously.

title: Pet Evacuation Capacity Options
one_liner: An annual small-fee option that reserves boarding capacity near you and pays for it automatically when an official evacuation order hits your address.
customer: Pet-owning households in wildfire, hurricane and flood zones, especially those on FAIR plans or recently nonrenewed. Homeowner insurers, brokers and HOAs are second buyers as a retention perk. Boarding kennels, vet clinics and pet-friendly hotels sell the reserved capacity.
problem: Pets are a leading reason people delay or refuse evacuation. In an evacuation the scarce resource is capacity, not money: pet-friendly shelters fill within hours and boarding facilities book out. Homeowners facing record nonrenewals have no cheap product to show insurers are still doing something for them, and kennels' unused capacity is perishable inventory.
solution: Sell an annual $49-79 option: reserved boarding slots (up to 14 days at a pre-agreed rate) at a vetted network within a 2-hour drive. It is triggered automatically when an official evacuation warning polygon covers the owner's address. Vaccination records are pre-verified so facilities accept the pet immediately. Facilities earn a retainer for reserving capacity plus a surge rate when exercised, paid instantly. Launch as a prepaid service reservation and convert to a parametric insurance structure through an MGA later.
why_now: Homeowner nonrenewals set records, California passed three claims and nonrenewal bills on Sept 3, and FAIR plans are growing. Reinsurance is softening with record cat-bond issuance, so parametric capacity is cheap. Instant payment rails exist, and late September is the run-up to peak fire and hurricane exposure.
revenue_model: Annual option premium, B2B2C fees of $10-20 per policy from insurers, brokers or HOAs, and a margin on surge-rate exercises.
non_obvious_insight: Sell a call option on capacity, not an insurance payout. In a crisis the value is in a guaranteed place to put the animal, and kennels would rather sell perishable capacity in advance than hope for demand. Parametric triggers make the whole thing automatic, which insurers love.
first_30_days: Pick one wildfire county. Sign 8 boarding facilities on a small retainer and pre-sell 300 households through fire-safe councils and HOAs. Build the trigger from public evacuation-zone feeds and run reservations manually the first season.

title: Humanoid Rentals for Events and Retail
one_liner: The first profitable humanoid job is spectacle: rent Unitree-class robots plus a trained show operator to brands, malls, arenas and trade shows.
customer: Experiential-marketing agencies, retail flagships, stadium and arena marketing teams, trade-show exhibitors, casinos and theme venues. Universities renting lab time come second.
problem: Everyone else pitches humanoids as factory workers, where reliability, safety and ROI are unproven. Brands want a 'robots are here' moment now but cannot buy, program and insure a $16k robot themselves.
solution: Own 6-10 units. Sell packaged experiences (greeter, product demo, dance or boxing, photo-booth persona) with an operator, choreographer, safety marshal and event insurance. Every event doubles as a demo funnel for enterprise pilot inquiries, and later as controlled data capture.
why_now: Unitree's August 2026 IPO (about $9B) and G1 pricing near $16k make fleet capex trivial, so a robot pays back in roughly 10 event-days at $1.5-2.5k a day (my estimate). Humanoid hype is at its peak and marketing budgets are chasing it. China's robot-rental-for-events market is a proof point.
revenue_model: $2-6k a day per robot with operator, $25-60k custom activations, and sponsorship fees. Add an enterprise-pilot lead-gen fee from robot vendors later.
non_obvious_insight: Entertainment tolerates a 70% success rate and teleop, because a stumble is content. The buyer pays for attention, not productivity, so humanoid economics work here years before they work on a factory floor. Note: tariffs or restrictions on Chinese robots are a risk, so keep a non-Chinese unit option.
first_30_days: Buy 2 G1s (about $32k) and build 3 scripted 10-minute acts. Cold-pitch 40 experiential agencies, minor-league teams and mall marketing managers. Book 5 paid weekend events and film content for social proof.

title: Battery-Free Soil Tags Read by Drone
one_liner: Disposable soil moisture and salinity tags that need no battery and are read by drone flyover.
customer: Agronomy service providers, co-ops and specialty-crop growers with irrigated fields.
problem: Farmers face fertilizer and diesel volatility with no pricing power, yet soil data stays sparse because sensors cost too much and need batteries.
solution: Sub-$3 ambient-backscatter tags placed at planting and read from a drone or planter-mounted reader, starting with moisture and salinity and adding nitrate later.
why_now: Ambient-IoT chips scaled in 2025, and urea swinging from $400 to $850 to about $453/t makes precise input use valuable.
revenue_model: Per-tag fee plus a per-acre mapping and reading service.
non_obvious_insight: Soil sampling stays sparse because sensors are expensive. Making them disposable makes dense maps feasible.
first_30_days: Buy ambient-IoT development kits, prove drone readout at short range, and run a small field pilot on two farms.

title: Designer Proteins for Clear Protein Water
one_liner: AI-designed acid-stable proteins that stay clear at pH 2.8-3.5, replacing whey in clear protein drinks.
customer: RTD beverage and sports-nutrition brands making clear protein waters.
problem: Whey uniquely gives clear drinks at pH 2.8-3.5, and no alternative matches it, so brands cannot swap out scarce whey.
solution: Computationally design candidate proteins for acid solubility and clarity, express them through a contract fermentation partner, and deliver a first clear-drink ingredient.
why_now: Protein-design models and cheap gene synthesis matured in 2025-26, and Verley's FDA-cleared fermentation whey shows the regulatory path for fermentation-derived proteins.
revenue_model: Development fees of $50-150k per brand, then per-kg supply or licensing.
non_obvious_insight: Alt-protein failed by trying to replicate all of dairy. The real gap is a single functionality in a single premium beverage format.
first_30_days: Design about 20 candidates, test solubility and turbidity at pH 3 with cell-free expression, and pitch 10 clear-protein brands for paid development.

title: Collateral Condition Reports for Farm Equipment
one_liner: Use newly opened Deere diagnostics to certify used-equipment condition for lenders and auctioneers handling a farm-distress wave.
customer: Community ag banks, Farm Credit associations, equipment auction houses and receivers.
problem: Farm bankruptcies are up 19% and row crops face a fourth loss-making year, so lenders are inheriting machinery they cannot value; poor condition data drives lowball auctions.
solution: An inspection product that reads fault history, engine and hydraulic hours and software status through independent diagnostic tools and issues a per-unit condition certificate, then builds valuation comps.
why_now: Deere's $99M settlement obliges it to open diagnostic and repair tools for 10 years, and repair restrictions cost farmers about $4.2B a year, so independent access is finally legitimate.
revenue_model: $250-600 per report, with annual subscriptions for lenders and per-lot fees from auction houses.
non_obvious_insight: Right-to-repair is framed as a farmer-savings story, but its most bankable use is collateral valuation for the lenders and auctioneers who must price distress.
first_30_days: Partner with three Midwest auction houses and two community banks, run 20 paid inspections using existing independent diagnostic tools, and publish sale-price comparisons.

title: Drone Hub Siting and Permit Intelligence
one_liner: Parcel-level zoning, noise and neighbor-risk scoring, plus done-for-you permit filing, for retailers and drone operators expanding launch hubs.
customer: Real-estate and expansion teams at retailers (Walmart, Lowe's, grocers, pharmacies), drone operators and delivery platforms such as Wing, Zipline and DoorDash, and regional chains entering drone delivery.
problem: Cities cannot regulate flight paths but can regulate launch hubs. Northglenn, for example, requires a special-use permit, a 200 ft residential buffer and no more than 65 dB at the property line. Walmart and Wing plan 270+ sites by 2027 (about 150 stores added in a year), and each is a separate local land-use fight.
solution: An LLM-parsed database of municipal zoning codes and drone ordinances, an acoustic model of hub operations, and parcel scoring (buffer, noise, neighbor density, HOA covenants) that outputs a go/no-go and a permit dossier. Add concierge filing and hearing prep. Also sell a model-ordinance toolkit to city planners.
why_now: Lowe's launched Wing/DoorDash delivery on September 28, 2026, and Walmart's rollout turns hub siting into a mass-production problem. With airspace approvals no longer the binding constraint, zoning boards are. LLMs make parsing thousands of local codes cheap.
revenue_model: $2-5k per site score, $10-25k per permit package, and $50-150k a year in enterprise SaaS. City licenses for the planning toolkit are a smaller add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The sky is federally preempted but the ground is local, so the scaling constraint has moved from the FAA to the zoning board. Whoever owns the ordinance graph decides where drone networks can expand, and both sides of the table will pay.
first_30_days: Scrape and structure drone-relevant ordinances for the top 150 municipalities in one high-growth state. Offer a free top-20 site scoring to a regional grocery or pharmacy chain, convert one paid permit package, and publish a model ordinance to generate city leads.

title: Orphan-Element Audits for Copper Concentrate and Tailings
one_liner: A 90-day survey that measures the tellurium, selenium, bismuth, cobalt, germanium, rhenium, indium and scandium copper mines already ship for free, then brokers by-product credit rights with refiners.
customer: Mid-size copper miners (Arizona, Utah, Nevada, Chile, Peru, Zambia, Kazakhstan) who sell concentrate to smelters or run SX-EW, paying $40-120k per site survey. Refiners and specialty-metal buyers (Aurubis-type smelters, Umicore, 5N Plus-type processors) pay finder fees. Government programmes such as DoD DPA Title III and DLA support recovery projects.
problem: Smelter contracts pay for Cu, Au and Ag. Te, Se, Bi, Co, Ge, In, Sb and Re are either given away, or shown only as penalty elements (As, Sb, Bi, Hg, F). The plant lab measures the penalty elements and stops. The 48-element ICP-MS suite exists only on exploration drill core from ten years ago and never on the concentrate, tailings, SX raffinate or electrolyte bleed streams. The smelter quietly captures value in anode slimes and flue dust. The miner has no data to negotiate with. Meanwhile, benchmark treatment charges for 2026 reportedly collapsed to around zero, so smelters are squeezed and newly hunting for by-product margin and for clean feed. Chinese export controls on Te, Bi, In, Ga, Ge, Sb and others make Western buyers desperate.
solution: A productised survey: pull 30-60 retained samples from process streams (every mine keeps monthly composite retains), run multi-element ICP-MS plus automated mineralogy through partner labs, and deliver an 'orphan-element balance' showing tonnes per year and contained value per element. Then hand the mine a negotiation kit: by-product participation clauses for offtake contracts, dust and slime credit language, and penalty-threshold renegotiation. Route the data to refiners and toll processors who can recover the element. The compensation is a survey fee plus 10-20% of by-product margin for 5 years, or a finder fee at contract signing.
why_now: In 2025 China imposed export controls on tellurium, bismuth, indium, gallium, germanium and antimony, with rare earths restrictions following. US and EU strategic stockpile, offtake and grant programmes now pay for domestic by-product supply. Smelters are under profit pressure from near-zero treatment charges and are open to sharing upside with suppliers. Prices for Te and Bi jumped.
revenue_model: $40-120k per site survey, plus a 10-20% by-product royalty or finder fee on recovered element revenue, plus a refiner-side subscription for a pipeline of quantified feed.
non_obvious_insight: The barrier is not technology. Kennecott has produced tellurium for decades. It is that nobody measured, so nobody owns the value, and contracts were signed when no one cared. The person who knows how the process streams flow (where it goes to anode slimes, where to dust) can tell which stream concentrates each element.
first_30_days: Ask ten friendly mid-tier mines for retained composite samples, or buy access to public tailings and concentrate assays. Run 15 multi-element packs at $60-150 each (about $2k in total). Produce a one-page 'value at stake' per mine and email it to 30 operations and commercial managers. Sell 2-3 pilot surveys at $25k. Meanwhile call two refiners and one federal programme office with the resulting map to line up demand.

title: Diabetes Desk: Remote Glucose-Curve Review for Clinics
one_liner: CGMs and once-daily insulins made diabetic pets manageable at home, but nobody owns the workflow; sell clinics an outsourced desk that reads curves and proposes titrations for the DVM to approve.
customer: General-practice clinics with a dozen or more insulin-dependent dogs and cats. Secondary: pet insurers with diabetic cohorts.
problem: AAHA's 2026 guidelines split canine and feline diabetes for the first time and emphasize CGMs and once-daily insulins (degludec, glargine U-300). Owner burden is high and remote-monitoring services are thin. Clinics get a stream of curves they have neither the time nor a billing model to review, so pets stay poorly regulated. Tight control gives diabetic cats a real chance of remission, and avoids expensive ketoacidosis emergencies.
solution: Owners link a CGM to a clinic-branded portal. A desk of RVTs plus a consulting internist reviews curves weekly, flags hypoglycemia risk, and drafts dose-change suggestions for the clinic's own vet to approve within their VCPR. Includes SMS coaching on feeding and injection technique and refill/supply coordination. The clinic bills the owner a monthly program fee and pays us a wholesale share.
why_now: 2026 AAHA guidelines make CGM standard-of-care thinking. Long-acting insulins reduce injection burden. Ambient AI makes the record-keeping cheap, and remote-care rules are loosening piecemeal.
revenue_model: Clinic charges owners $59-99 per month; we take about $30-45 per patient per month. Later: outcome-based contracts with insurers.
non_obvious_insight: The clinical tech (CGMs, insulins, guidelines) arrived before the operating model. Human remote-monitoring took years to get billing codes; in vet medicine the owner pays directly and the value (fewer ER visits) is visible immediately, so a desk business can start without any payer.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 clinics and about 20 diabetic patients. Run a manual desk with one contract RVT and a part-time internist consult. Use CGM sharing links or screenshots to start. Track time-in-range and ER visits, and price the pilot at $79 per month.

title: Neutral Caninization Platform for Pet Antibody Drugs
one_liner: A species-adaptation and developability service that lets animal-health companies without Zoetis's proprietary platform make dog, cat and horse antibody drugs.
customer: Mid-size animal-health companies (Elanco, Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health, Merck Animal Health, Dechra, Ceva, Virbac, Asian vet-pharma) and pet-biotech startups.
problem: Companion-animal mAbs (Cytopoint, Librela, Solensia, Lenivia, Portela) are dominated by one player with roughly 85-90% of revenue, built on a proprietary caninization platform. Others cannot reliably turn a validated human target into a dog- or cat-ready antibody with proper Fc biology, FcRn-driven half-life and low anti-drug-antibody risk. AI binder-design tools are trained on human and mouse data, not canine or feline.
solution: Offer (1) canine, feline and equine germline-framework and Fc libraries with species-specific FcRn and FcgR binding assays, (2) AI-assisted binder design and caninization against validated pet targets (IL-31, NGF, IL-4/13, CD20, PD-1), (3) canine PBMC and ADA-risk screens, and (4) a lead plus data package for USDA or FDA-CVM pathways. Sell as fixed-price programs.
why_now: 2026 review literature names species adaptation and Fc biology as the missing platform pieces. Zero-shot AI antibody design has reached double-digit hit rates, so making binders is cheap while species adaptation is the moat. Zoetis's pet-mAb franchise proves the commercial size, and FDA's expanded conditional approval for major species (through 2028) is available.
revenue_model: $150-400k per program plus milestones and deliberately light royalties, and reagent sales (species-specific FcRn and receptor kits).
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume AI-designed drugs must prove themselves in human oncology. Animal health has smaller and faster trials, direct-pay owners and a concentrated incumbent whose moat is the platform, not the targets. AI attacks exactly that platform. The first AI-designed antibody drug on the market may well be for dogs.
first_30_days: Build canine and feline framework and Fc reagent sets from public sequences and gene synthesis (~$20k). Run FcRn binding on 10 published veterinary mAbs to show calibration. Pitch 15 animal-health BD leads and 5 pet-biotech startups. Sign 1-2 paid feasibility studies ($30-60k), such as caninizing a validated human target.

title: Customs-Verified Collateral for Inventory Lenders
one_liner: An API and reporting layer that verifies borrowers' in-transit inventory against ISF, entry, release and liquidation records, so lenders stop financing containers that do not exist.
customer: Inventory-finance and revenue-based lenders for e-commerce brands, factoring companies, ABL desks at small banks, and buyers of tariff-refund receivables. They pay per verification and per monitored loan.
problem: Lenders finance purchase orders and goods on the water. Their collateral evidence is invoices, a bill of lading PDF and the borrower's word. Fraud, double-pledging, inflated quantities and phantom shipments are a chronic loss driver in small-business trade finance. Tariffs made it worse: duties now consume a big share of landed cost, so lenders need to know what was actually declared, at what value, and whether it cleared or is held. The truth exists in CBP data that brokers see within hours. Lenders see it, if at all, weeks late through the borrower.
solution: Connect to the collateral through consent-based data paths: importer-scheduled ACE reports forwarded to a dedicated inbox, and ABI/status feeds from cooperating brokers that get paid for sharing. Reconcile each financed PO against ISF filing, entry summary, release or hold status, declared value and HTS, and (after the IEEPA ruling) refund eligibility. Deliver a loan-level 'entry-verified' status and exception alerts, such as a container that never had an ISF, a value mismatch, or an exam hold that makes collateral illiquid. The same engine verifies IEEPA refund claims for lenders advancing against them.
why_now: Inventory financing and tariff-duty financing for e-commerce brands surged in 2024-26, and lenders are absorbing losses they do not yet understand. Refund-backed lending is new since the Feb 2026 IEEPA ruling and CAPE, and it needs entry-level verification. ACE reports are self-serve, so no permission from CBP is needed. Brokers are looking for revenue beyond thin filing fees.
revenue_model: $15-40 per shipment verification, or a monitoring SaaS fee of about 5-15 basis points on funded volume, with platform minimums of $2-5k a month. Brokers get a revenue share on data feeds. Add-on: refund-claim diligence packages.
non_obvious_insight: A PO and a bill of lading are easy to forge. An ISF filed before vessel loading, tied to a bond, followed by a release message from CBP, is not. It is the closest thing to a government-attested proof that goods exist and are moving. Because the importer owns the ACE data, no data-broker licensing fight is needed. Trade-finance software vendors model documents. Nobody models the entry record.
first_30_days: Approach five small inventory lenders, factors and refund-claim buyers with a manual pilot: they send 10 borrowers' entry data, and you return verified and unverified lists within 48 hours. Recruit two friendly customs brokers for feed access on consenting clients. Build the reconciliation on spreadsheets and scripts first, and charge $500-$1,500 per pilot batch. The first paid lender contract is usually a covenant addition: 'borrower must forward ACE reports monthly'.

title: Price-Raise Autopilot for One-Person Service Firms
one_liner: Find the underpriced clients in a solo operator's own invoice history and execute personalized price increases, paid as a share of the uplift.
customer: Nonemployer and 1-5 person service businesses with 50-800 repeat clients: groomers, cleaners, landscapers, bookkeepers, tutors, therapists, detailers.
problem: Rising costs are the top financial challenge, yet most solo operators have not repriced in years because they fear churn. The industry sells lead generation, not repricing, even though a modest increase on the bottom 40% of clients often beats a 20% lift in leads.
solution: Connect Stripe, Square, QuickBooks, Jobber or booking-software history. For each client, compute the effective hourly rate after drive time, materials and discounts, and rank clients as safe-to-raise or protect. Draft one-to-one messages in the owner's voice, send by text or email, track churn and replies, and roll back individual clients if needed. The dashboard shows before-and-after profit per hour.
why_now: The Fed's 2026 survey shows 76% of international sourcers already passed costs to customers, so consumers now accept increases. Payment and booking APIs give clean multi-year history, and LLMs write natural personal notes at zero marginal cost.
revenue_model: 15-20% of first-year incremental revenue captured (no uplift, no fee), or a $49/month plan for owners who prefer flat pricing.
non_obvious_insight: The industry assumes the number-one problem, getting customers, is the one to fix. For a business of one, the fastest path to profit is charging existing customers correctly, and owners are too close to their clients to do it themselves. Outcome pricing also works because the owner sees the money.
first_30_days: Run a concierge version for 20 groomers, cleaners and landscapers found in local Facebook groups, using exports and spreadsheets. Measure revenue lift and churn below 3%. Publish two before-and-after case studies and use them to price the software.

title: Tariff Surcharge Clawback for Downstream Buyers
one_liner: A contingency recovery-audit firm that claws back tariff surcharges buyers paid on duties their suppliers have since had refunded.
customer: CFOs, AP and purchasing teams at $20M-$1B manufacturers and distributors that paid itemized supplier 'tariff surcharges' in 2025-26.
problem: The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20. By 2026-07-10 CBP had accepted about $121.75B in claims and repaid about $86.3B. Many suppliers billed explicit surcharges (one shop-floor post cites 2.7%) to fund those duties, and they are now collecting refunds on the same money. Buyers assume the refund belongs to the importer of record, and AP treats surcharge lines as noise.
solution: Ingest 18 months of AP data from the ERP or QuickBooks. Use LLM extraction on invoices and price-increase emails to find surcharge lines. Rank suppliers by likely refunded exposure (product HTS and the IEEPA rate window). Generate credit-memo demands and negotiation scripts. Escalate to counsel only for large amounts. Recovery depends on invoice and contract language, and most cases settle as credits against future invoices.
why_now: Refunds are paying out in phases right now, so suppliers hold the cash today. Contract dispute windows are open and evidence is fresh.
revenue_model: 20-30% contingency fee on recovered cash or credits. Optional $5k flat fee for a scan of the last 12 months of AP.
non_obvious_insight: The strongest and cheapest claim to a refund often belongs to the downstream buyer holding an itemized surcharge, not the importer. Recovery-audit firms hunt duplicate payments, not tariffs. Buyers also avoid asking for fear of damaging the supplier relationship, so an anonymous third party has an edge.
first_30_days: Sign 5 mid-market manufacturers for a free 12-month surcharge scan. Have counsel draft one template letter. Send the first demands and measure realized recovery. First credit memos should land within 60-90 days.

title: Peer-Made Aide Training in Creole, Spanish, Tagalog
one_liner: A library of short scenario videos made by experienced home-care aides in their own languages, RN-reviewed and sold to agencies as required in-service training that keeps new aides from quitting.
customer: Home-care agencies, home health agencies and nursing homes in immigrant-heavy states (NY, FL, MA, NJ, CA). The buyer is the training or HR lead, paying per aide.
problem: Agency turnover runs 77-80% and roughly 4 in 5 new caregivers quit within 100 days. 30% of direct care workers are immigrants (60% in New York), and about 350,000 Haitians lost TPS on Aug 4. Federal rules require annual in-service hours for home health aides and nursing-home nurse aides (12 hours a year, and states add more), and most content is English-language corporate e-learning or AI-dubbed avatars that workers ignore and that can be clinically wrong.
solution: Recruit working aides who already post in Haitian Creole, Spanish, Tagalog or Arabic on Facebook, TikTok and WhatsApp. They shoot 3 to 6 minute scenarios (transfers, dementia redirection, refusing a bath, safe lifting). An RN reviews each script, and the clip carries a 'peer-made, RN-verified' provenance stamp. The platform adds quizzes, attendance logs for surveyors, and a first-week mentor-video track aimed at the 100-day cliff. Creators get 35-40% of revenue plus a bonus for completion.
why_now: Visa pauses and TPS terminations are reshuffling the workforce by language group right now. The federal nursing-home staffing mandate was repealed (Feb 2026), which leaves retention as the agencies' only lever. AI slop training content is flooding the market, and creators are hunting for income beyond ad revenue.
revenue_model: $9-14 per aide per month billed to the agency (a 75-aide agency pays about $700-1,000), sold as an annual contract. About 35-40% goes to creators. A later add-on covers state-approved CE credits and dementia-training modules.
non_obvious_insight: Aides do not quit because training is bad. They quit because nobody who looks or sounds like them says the job gets easier. A peer in your language who has survived the first 100 days is a retention device that also happens to satisfy a compliance line item, and an AI avatar cannot supply that credibility.
first_30_days: Find 5 aide-creators through Creole, Spanish and Tagalog Facebook groups and workforce training programs. Partner with a per-diem RN reviewer. Shoot 20 scenarios in 3 weeks and pitch 5 agencies (start with Miami, Boston and NYC) on a 90-day pilot at a free-first-month price tied to a measured 100-day retention improvement.

title: Audit-Grade Inventory Robots for Defense Property
one_liner: Drone and rover inventory counts that produce tamper-evident audit evidence, sold first to defense contractors who must physically inventory government-furnished property, then to Pentagon depots racing a clean-audit deadline.
customer: Property managers at small and mid-size defense contractors (machine shops, depot-level repair firms, integrators holding government property). Later, DoD depots and audit-readiness contractors that need count observation.
problem: DoD has never passed a full financial audit and has set a clean-opinion goal of about 2028 (verify), and inventory and materiel existence are among the biggest obstacles. Leaders admit they lack supply-chain data to support a '90-, 120-, 180-day fight'. Federal staff capacity is shrinking (OPM rating caps, contested reorganizations) and agencies keep buying capacity. Contractors holding government property (FAR 52.245-1) must keep records and do periodic physical inventories that DCMA property administrators review, and the work is manual and labor-heavy.
solution: Deploy indoor drones, rovers and wearable scanners to produce time-stamped, geotagged, hash-chained count evidence reconciled to property records. Output exception lists in the format auditors and property administrators expect. Use offline-first, air-gapped operation, since air-gap-native tooling (Defense Unicorns) cut authorization from 18 months to about 2 weeks. Begin in low-hazard bays and add ordnance-safe hardware later.
why_now: Warehouse inventory drones matured in commercial logistics but were never packaged for federal audit evidence. The Pentagon's comfort with small drones jumped through Drone Dominance, and audit-readiness spending is a live budget line. Federal staffing cuts push work to contractors.
revenue_model: Per verified location or per count event, priced below manual count crews, with annual recurring programs for contractors. Later, per-depot audit-evidence programs through subcontracts.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is not logistics but the CFO and audit-readiness office, which has a statutory deadline and money, while logistics chiefs have no robot budget. Selling robots as 'audit evidence' unlocks the funding. Contractor-held government property is a commercial beachhead with a private budget.
first_30_days: Recruit two defense contractors with large government-property holdings and one small audit or property-compliance firm. Do a free count at one facility to define the evidence format. Then price a paid annual inventory at each and pursue a small DLA or Army innovation solicitation.

title: Hyperspectral Target Packs for Natural Hydrogen Explorers
one_liner: Use newly open hyperspectral satellite data to rank licence blocks for natural hydrogen, then sell the evidence pack that helps cash-poor explorers raise money and keep their licences.
customer: Junior explorers and startups holding or applying for natural-hydrogen licences (ASX/TSXV juniors, private startups, landmen leasing in the US Midcontinent, Spain, France, South Australia and the Philippines), plus government surveys running tenders.
problem: Licences and leases are being granted essentially blind in a land rush. Drilling costs millions, and the only surface clues are ultramafic and iron-rich rock, vegetation anomalies and circular depressions. Small explorers cannot afford a full geophysics programme yet need credible evidence for investors and regulators.
solution: A multi-sensor prospectivity pack: hyperspectral mineral mapping (EMIT, Planet Tanager open data, Pixxel tasking) for serpentinized ultramafic rocks and iron-oxide and clay alteration; multi-year vegetation-stress anomalies; Sentinel-2 and SAR detection of circular depressions; then public gravity/magnetics and geology. Output is a ranked block list and a 20-page evidence deck, with an optional partner ground-truth soil-gas hydrogen survey.
why_now: Koloma has raised about $400M and won the first competitive natural-hydrogen bid round in the Philippines (three contracts, over 4,000 km2). A USGS map, DOE grants, EU funding (Mantle 8) and Australian co-funding are all live. Open hyperspectral archives (EMIT, Tanager) and cheap commercial tasking (Pixxel Firefly, about $8/km2 quoted) did not exist three years ago.
revenue_model: $10k to $40k per licence-block pack. $3k to $8k a month monitoring retainer. For cash-poor juniors, part-payment via a small royalty or option in place of cash.
non_obvious_insight: In a gold rush, the scarce product is a credible map that makes the pitch deck and licence renewal defensible, and hyperspectral is unusually good at the specific rock chemistry of serpentinization. You sell ranking plus a ground-truth feedback loop, not certainty, and each drill or soil-gas result improves the model in a way competitors cannot copy.
first_30_days: Back-test on known hydrogen occurrences and known fairy-circle areas to measure hit rate. Publish a free prospectivity map of one region (Kansas/Nebraska Midcontinent Rift or South Australia) to attract leads. Sell three packs to ASX or TSXV juniors at $10k to $15k.

title: App-Diet Service for the Phone-Upgrade Freeze
one_liner: As phones get unaffordable, today's handset becomes a five-year handset, so old-device performance decides who keeps users.
customer: Banks, wallets, telcos and government digital services with large user bases on 2-3GB RAM Android phones in Africa, India and LatAm.
problem: Memory-driven price rises are stretching replacement cycles. Bloated apps crash on old devices, and churn from that is invisible in analytics.
solution: A fixed-price audit on a real farm of used 2GB phones on 2G/3G. Deliver sub-10MB lite builds and WhatsApp or USSD fallbacks, then a monthly regression retainer. The wedge is a four-week audit for one mid-tier bank or wallet.
why_now: Memory is 30-40% of phone cost, LatAm shipments fell 10%, and GSMA's $40 phone pilot shows the price problem.
revenue_model: $15-40k per audit and $5-10k per month for device-lab monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone forecasts the next phone. The second-order effect is that the current phone lasts far longer, so performance on old hardware, not features, drives retention.
first_30_days: Buy 15 used phones and publish a teardown of the top 10 fintech apps in Nigeria or India. Use it to book audits.

title: Notice Red-Team and Pleading Triage for Landlords
one_liner: An adversarial checker that tries to break every eviction notice before it is served, then triages incoming AI-drafted pleadings and prices cash-for-keys exits.
customer: Mid-size operators (500-10,000 units) and the landlord-tenant law firms that serve them on flat-fee matters.
problem: Federal pro se filings topped 41,000 in 2025 against a 23,000 average for 2005-2022, and one tenant filed 22 pleadings in a weekend. Operators pay outside counsel to triage each one while units sit idle, and some conclude cash-for-keys is cheaper than winning. Tenants' AI can find a defective notice in minutes, so procedural errors are now fatal.
solution: An adversarial reviewer checks each notice (cure periods, statutory language, service method, ledger accuracy including banned fees) against jurisdiction rules before service. Inbound pleadings are classified, deadlines docketed, and a 48-hour decision brief compares cost-to-contest with a benchmarked cash-for-keys offer that respects relocation rules. An evidence pack (ledger, communications, inspection logs) is auto-assembled. Licensed attorneys supervise, to avoid unauthorized-practice risk.
why_now: Generative tools have made pro se filings cheap and voluminous, and operators are shrinking staff and leaning on AI leasing, so their record-keeping is thin. Municipal fee bans add new ways a ledger can be wrong.
revenue_model: $3-6 per unit per year platform fee plus $75-250 per triaged matter; law-firm seats at $300-600 per month.
non_obvious_insight: The real cost is not the pleading but the vacant unit while it sits in dispute, so the winning metric is decision speed inside 48 hours. Both sides are now AI-armed, and the defensible edge is an adversarial 'red team' that finds your process defects before the tenant does.
first_30_days: Partner with two landlord-tenant firms in a high-volume market. Build a notice checker for two jurisdictions and run it free on 200 historical notices to show catch-rates. Convert firms to a $500 per month seat and operators to a per-matter fee.

title: Guard-Shack Handshake: Stopping Fictitious Pickups at the Gate
one_liner: A free, no-login gate tool for shipper guard shacks that shows the pre-enrolled driver, truck, plate and a one-time PIN, paid for per protected load by brokers and cargo insurers.
customer: Brokers moving high-theft commodities (electronics, copper and other metals, consumer goods, food and beverage) and their cargo and contingent-cargo insurers pay. Shippers get the guard tool free, which is what drives adoption.
problem: CargoNet estimates H1 2026 cargo theft losses above $359M, with Q2 2026 losses of $304.6M (more than double Q2 2025) even though incidents fell, driven by high-value metals and technology. Criminals now compromise legitimate carrier accounts, internet-based phone systems, email and compliance-platform credentials, so the email domain, callback number and vetting badge can all be authentic-looking. Meanwhile at the physical gate a guard checks a load number and a BOL, as in 1995. The load number is a password that the broker has already emailed to dozens of carriers.
solution: At tender, the broker's rate-con flow triggers a driver self-enrollment via SMS link: selfie, CDL photo, truck and trailer plate photos. The system checks how recently the carrier's public contact info changed and whether the enrolling number matches prior loads. The shipper's shipping desk and guard get a web link (no app, no integration) showing the expected driver photo, plate and USDOT number. The driver must speak a PIN issued only through the enrollment. The guard taps match or mismatch and snaps an arrival photo, and any mismatch alerts the broker and shipper instantly. The receiver gets the same flow at delivery. Aggregated data goes to insurers.
why_now: The 2026 CargoNet reports describe impersonation-based theft as systematic and scalable, with credential and phone-system compromise defeating digital-only checks. Montgomery (May 2026) raised broker liability, and insurers are now asking brokers for controls. The Jan 2026 FMCSA rule means a broker who pays a big theft claim can drop below the bond threshold and face suspension.
revenue_model: $2-$5 per protected load charged to brokers, plus an insurer revenue share or bounty for verified low-loss books. Later, sell a 'verified pickup' certificate to cargo insurers in exchange for lower deductibles.
non_obvious_insight: The thief needs two things, a load number and a plausible carrier identity, and the broker hands out both freely. Nobody has redesigned the 30-second guard-shack transaction because shippers feel the cargo is no longer theirs once the BOL is signed, so the party that eats the loss (broker or insurer) has to fund a free tool for the party that controls the gate. The best fraud tell is not the carrier's score but the age of its contact info: hijacked carriers show new phones and emails days before booking. Brokers whisper this in fraud groups but no product sells it.
first_30_days: Sign 3 brokers hauling metals or electronics and pick 5 recurring shipper docks. Build a web-only MVP (SMS enrollment plus guard view) and run the PINs manually. Pilot 100 loads, measuring driver friction (target under 90 seconds) and catch rate with seeded red-team tests. Get one cargo insurer or MGA to review the pilot data for a premium credit.

title: Actual-Play Sessions Turned Into Animated Episodes
one_liner: A pipeline that turns a tabletop RPG stream's audio and character art into a condensed animated episode using the cast's own voices, with human review.
customer: Actual-play shows and TTRPG creators with 3k-50k Patreon patrons, and TTRPG publishers wanting marketing series.
problem: Fans want animated adaptations, but animation costs millions. Creators have hundreds of hours of audio and no way to give patrons a visual product.
solution: Ingest the session audio and each creator's character art bible. An LLM editor condenses a 4-hour session into a 12-20 minute script. Video generation uses per-character references trained only on the creator's own art, with consenting voices and lip-sync, and a producer reviews each cut. Output includes premium-tier episodes and short clips for growth.
why_now: Video models now generate consistent characters with synced audio, and creators can use their own art and voices with disclosure, which sidesteps most of the AI-slop backlash.
revenue_model: $1.5-5k per episode or 20-30% of new patron revenue for 12 months, plus a licensing fee for publishers.
non_obvious_insight: The output is not cinema but the recap format, the 'previously on' fans share, and the same pipeline produces shorts that grow the channel. Consent and disclosure are the differentiators.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 mid-size actual-play creators. Produce one 90-second pilot for each from public sessions, and refine. Sell 3 paid episodes at $1.5k.

title: Retiree Remote-Assist Bench for Robot Fleets
one_liner: A certified, US-based, part-time pool of retirees (ex-truckers, dispatchers, yard hands) who resolve robot and AV exceptions, billed by the assisted hour to fleet operators.
customer: Operators of driverless trucks, yard-automation systems, delivery robots and warehouse fleets (Bot Auto, Gatik, YardFlow-style deployments, sidewalk-robot firms), paying $45-65 per assisted hour.
problem: Every fleet needs remote humans for edge cases. Waymo alone runs about 70 agents on shift, partly in the Philippines, and offshore assist is now a political and first-responder question (NHTSA letter, Jul 2026). Meanwhile 65+ workers want flexible seated income and have the domain judgment, for example reading a truck yard or a weigh station.
solution: Recruit and train retirees on a common exception-handling curriculum. Certify them per vehicle or robot type. Supply them as a managed bench with scheduling, QA and a US-based, background-checked compliance story. Retirees earn $28-40 an hour for 10-20 hours a week, which keeps them under Social Security earnings limits.
why_now: Driverless freight went early-commercial in 2026 (Aurora about 200 trucks, Gatik 85k orders). Fleets are scaling remote-assist headcount, and regulators are scrutinizing where it sits.
revenue_model: Managed-service margin: bill $45-65 per hour, pay $28-40, keep about 35% gross margin. Add training and certification fees per operator.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input for autonomy is not more compute. It is cheap, trustworthy human judgment on demand. The demographic everyone treats as a care burden is the best-matched supply of that judgment.
first_30_days: Pitch two mid-size operators for a paid pilot in one metro (freight yards, sidewalk robots). Recruit 25 retired CDL drivers and dispatchers via trucker associations and AARP groups. Run a two-week training and bill the pilot at cost-plus.
